title: Local Homophily-Aware Graph Neural Network with Adaptive Polynomial Filters for Scalable Graph Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Graph anomaly detection must model a complex interplay of homophily and heterophily, with anomalous nodes typically exhibiting greater heterophily than normal nodes.

gap.claim: Existing GNN-based methods face computational inefficiency from spectral decomposition and difficulty estimating node-wise local homophily without prior homophily information.

contributions.claim: LH-GNN uses a lightweight polynomial graph filter that dynamically adjusts to node-specific homophily ratios through adaptable heterophilic and homophilic bases.
LH-GNN uses iterative prototype learning with class prototypes and uncertainty measures to estimate local homophily and assign pseudolabels without additional labels.
The framework is designed for linear time complexity and scalable graph anomaly detection.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present LH-GNN as a novel graph anomaly detection framework and identify its adaptive polynomial filtering and iterative prototype learning innovations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four benchmark datasets reportedly show that LH-GNN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in effectiveness and efficiency.
The authors report a 4.4% improvement in detection accuracy.
The authors report an 11× computational speedup.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph anomalies involve differing homophily and heterophily patterns, with anomalous nodes typically more heterophilic.
Prior methods are limited by expensive spectral computation and unavailable node-wise homophily ratios.
LH-GNN combines adaptive polynomial filtering with iterative prototype-based local homophily estimation.
The authors report gains in detection accuracy and computational speed across four benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: Anomaly detection may benefit from node-specific handling of homophilic and heterophilic structure.

interpretation.claim: A single globally fixed graph propagation behavior may be insufficient when structural similarity varies across nodes.

application.claim: For graph anomaly detection, consider adaptive local structural filters combined with uncertainty-aware pseudo-labeling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers to graphs whose anomaly patterns or homophily distributions differ from the reported benchmarks.

unknowns: The four benchmark datasets are not identified.
The evaluation metrics, baselines, and experimental protocol are not specified.
The abstract does not provide details supporting the linear-time complexity claim.
